classification.difficultyReason: Express one square face area as s squared and generalise to six equal faces to form the surface-area formula.

content.prompt: What would be the formula for the surface area of a cube with side length $s$?

spec.description: Cube with front, top and right faces visible, three hidden edges and three side-length labels; decorative grey fills omitted.
spec.mathematics: All cube edges have length s.

answer.worked:
The cube has six square faces, each with area $s^2$.
$$\begin{align*}SA&=6\times s^2\\SA&=6s^2\end{align*}$$
